solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I'm afraid to return power to guard

indicators.note: to return means the exclamation is read backwards, from its end to its start

parts.note: eek is the squeak of someone frightened
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A nervous security guard admits being scared to go back on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something is to protect or watch over it, as a guard does.

clue.text: Cabbage hearts; I save 50 fine boxes up!

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole string is read from bottom to top
boxes means encloses, so the letter for hearts goes inside

parts.note: bar and save both mean except
L is the Roman numeral for 50
OK means fine, all right
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A gardener saves cabbage hearts and packs them in boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: I, BAR, L, OK box H, giving IBARLHOK, which read upwards spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a variety of the cabbage family grown for its swollen stem.

clue.text: The heart of very wicked sexologist

indicators.note: the heart of means the outer letters are dropped, keeping the middle

parts.note: hellish means extremely bad or evil

explanation.surface: A specialist in sexual behaviour is found to be wicked at the core.
explanation.walkthrough: Havelock Ellis was an English pioneer of the study of human sexuality.
explanation.definitionFit: Havelock Ellis wrote influential studies of human sexual psychology, a founding figure of that science.

clue.text: On holiday that's very sweet indeed

parts.note: aw is the cooing exclamation at something cute
ay is an old or dialect form of yes, an emphatic agreement

explanation.surface: Someone on a trip finds the place utterly charming.
explanation.walkthrough: This answer begins a message across the top row: KEEP AWAY FROM CHILDREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is away is absent from home, as a person on vacation is.

clue.text: Pleasant women at home — that will do this man!

parts.note: in means at home
so said firmly closes a matter, as in so, that settles it
me is the setter referring to himself

explanation.surface: A man boasts that charming homely women will win him over.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means attractive and charming, an engaging quality.

clue.text: Together, "surly" and "objectionable" would describe him

indicators.note: together means the two quoted words are run into one string, and the tail of the first is used at the join
would describe asks for only the bit of the second word that meets the join, so the rest of it falls away

parts.note: only its opening pair of letters, the part that meets the join, is kept

explanation.surface: A sour and offensive man is summed up in two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A yob is a loutish young thug, typically rude and unpleasant.

clue.text: Out of class with upset stomach?

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle of the word, and upset turns those two central letters over

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A pupil is sent home from lessons with a tummy bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The stomach of FORM is its centre, OR; upsetting it gives RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both prepositions express origin or source, as in taken from a box or out of a box.

clue.text: Fellow, lying at the outset, broaching fairies dancing?

definitions.text: Fellow, lying at the outset, broaching fairies dancing?

indicators.note: broaching means piercing, so the letter enters the shuffled word
dancing means the letters of fairies move about
at the outset means the first letter of lying

explanation.surface: A man tells fibs, beginning by claiming to have seen fairies dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsifier is one who lies or fakes, and a man claiming dancing fairies is spinning untruths.

clue.text: Result of Erling's header breaking deadlock? Yes and no

definitions.text: Result of Erling's header breaking deadlock? Yes and no

parts.words: Result of Erling's header breaking deadlock? Yes and no
parts.note: a level score after the striker scores: deadlock is broken, then restored, so yes and no

explanation.walkthrough: Erling Haaland is Manchester City's striker. The blogger read E (Erling's header) as both within and outside ON ON; a commenter suggested E breaking NONE-NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-all scoreline is a draw, so the game stays level, still a stalemate of sorts.

clue.text: A problem to decipher lamentation read over Mass

parts.note: a cry is a wail of grief
PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to go over the page
a gram is a unit of mass

explanation.surface: A grieving cry is read aloud over a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogram is a coded text, a puzzle that must be cracked to read.

clue.text: Kids caught with feet up on back of ottoman

parts.note: chill'd, the poetic past tense of chill, means both caught (a cold) and relaxed with your feet up; it sounds like the word for a kid
re means on, concerning

indicators.note: back of means only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Children are found lounging with their feet resting on a footstool.
explanation.walkthrough: Chilled does double duty: relaxing with feet up, and caught (a chill). The setter takes it as the clipped form CHILL'D, which is said like CHILD; then RE and the N at the end of ottoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Kids is informal for young people, sons and daughters.

clue.text: Who's showing poise capturing Odette's heart by Lake — and Siegfried's finale?

definitions.text: Who's showing poise capturing Odette's heart by Lake — and Siegfried's finale?

indicators.note: capturing means the next letters are held inside the word for one who keeps poise

parts.note: a balancer is one who keeps steady and poised
L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: heart means the central letters of the name Odette

parts.note: the central pair of letters of the name, the 's being possessive

indicators.note: finale means the last letter of the name Siegfried

parts.note: the final letter of the name is taken, the 's being possessive

explanation.surface: Who, with grace, wins the heart of Odette in Swan Lake, as Siegfried does at its end?
explanation.walkthrough: Odette and Prince Siegfried are the lovers in Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake, so the whole clue also describes the man dancing Siegfried.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer in classical ballet holds poise, and the one dancing Siegfried wins Odette's heart on stage.

clue.text: Take this for granted: "Full pint in hand, elbow bent, waiting to toast …"

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an assumption taken for granted beforehand

definitions.text: Full pint in hand, elbow bent, waiting to toast …
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: the ..., the stance just before supping a drink

explanation.surface: A drinker stands ready, glass raised, about to give a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as PRE-SUP POSITION: the posture held before you sup.
explanation.definitionFit: A presupposition is an assumption made in advance, something taken for granted before reasoning begins.

clue.text: The low-down on a nudist's nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Gossip about a naturist's private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The low-down is the inside information, all the details of how something works.

clue.text: Gun-belt my boss is wearing followed emergency procedures?

definitions.text: Gun-belt my boss is wearing followed emergency procedures?

parts.words: Gun-belt my boss is wearing followed emergency procedures?
parts.note: the opening words describe a strap worn at the waist of the editor, the setter's boss; respaced, the phrase for leaving a sinking vessel says just that

explanation.surface: An office worker describes the holster strapped to their manager.
explanation.walkthrough: Respace the answer as A BAND ON ED'S HIP; the editor (Ed) is the setter's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving a sinking vessel by order of the captain is the classic emergency procedure at sea.

clue.text: Like a beautiful maiden in lacy pants snorting speed

indicators.note: snorting means taking in, so the shuffled letters draw in the speed unit
pants means rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be rearranged

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A lingerie-clad girl takes amphetamine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph in myth is a lovely young maiden spirit, and this adjective describes her.

clue.text: For Spooner, this would be just mere monogamy

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of two words, so the initial consonants change places

parts.note: bare means just, merely
a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs that marriage to one partner is nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: BARE POND swapped gives PARE BOND, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair bond is the exclusive lasting partnership of two mates, so it is a relationship of one partner.

clue.text: Opening the morning paper is fine — and ideal for Biden

indicators.note: opening means the following words are placed inside, splitting the newspaper words apart

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for the morning, ante meridiem
a ream is a quantity of paper
an eric was a fine paid for murder in old Irish law

explanation.surface: Someone happily opens the breakfast newspaper and finds all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: An eric is an obscure word: in old Irish law, a fine paid by a killer to the victim's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Biden is a US president, and the national aspiration of success through effort is the ideal of every American.

clue.text: One does wow a holder of securities!

parts.note: a char is a cleaner, one who does for a household
gee is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at a person who keeps stocks and bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is British for a cleaner; to do for someone is to clean their house.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargee holds a charge, a legal claim over property as security for a debt.

clue.text: A fool topped with British fruit

indicators.note: topped with means the next letter is placed on top in this down entry

parts.note: a nana is a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: A fruit fool dessert is crowned with a British topping.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is also a creamy fruit pudding, so the surface looks culinary.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a long yellow tropical produce item that grows in bunches.

clue.text: Fax Murdoch's organisation, pressing the old man to film

indicators.note: pressing means the next letters push in among the shuffled ones
organisation means the letters are arranged into a fresh order

parts.note: the words Fax Murdoch, the 's only possessive, shuffled as one pool of letters
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A demand to send a fax to Murdoch's media empire, urging Dad towards the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chump at Oxford is a 1940 Laurel and Hardy comedy; Murdoch is the media owner.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is that of a feature by the comedy pair Laurel and Hardy, a motion picture.

clue.text: Wild South African ostrich strangely excluded from this?

definitions.text: Wild South African ostrich strangely excluded from this?

indicators.note: wild means the letters run free to be rearranged
strangely excluded from means the letters of ostrich are taken out of the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: Puzzling that a native ostrich is missing from the local wildlife list.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna means the animals of a region, which would surely include the ostrich of southern Africa.

clue.text: See 10
Official who's mobbed by Tranmere fans

indicators.note: mobbed by means surrounded by, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A match official is surrounded by angry Tranmere supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Tranmere Rovers is an English football club near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is the official who enforces the rules in a match.

clue.text: Escape returning mist, engulfing European solicitor

indicators.note: engulfing means the reversed weather word swallows the next letters
returning means the weather word is read backwards

parts.note: fog is a thick mist
a tout solicits custom, so is one who solicits

explanation.surface: A traveller slips away in the fog, though a lawyer from Europe is caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: This begins the message along the bottom row: GET OUT OF JAIL FREE CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To get out of a duty or place is to avoid or flee it, a verbal phrase for escaping.

clue.text: Superb parts in short Ms Lopez put in the can

indicators.note: parts means the next letters split the shortened name in two
short means the last letter of the nickname is dropped

parts.note: JLo is the nickname of the singer Jennifer Lopez
A1 means first-rate, written here with I for the 1

explanation.surface: A first-rate performance by Jennifer Lopez is filmed and canned.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written as AI, letter I standing for the figure 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The can is slang for prison, so putting someone there is to imprison them.

clue.text: Courier's last wage packets to deliver

indicators.note: packets means wraps up, so the payment word encloses the letter

parts.note: a fee is a payment for work

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of the word courier is taken

parts.note: the word courier, its 's only possessive

explanation.surface: A delivery driver's final pay is sent as parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger is to rescue or liberate them.

clue.text: Eccentric motorist steering clear of river

indicators.note: steering clear of means avoiding, so the river word is taken out

parts.note: a motorist is a car driver

explanation.surface: An oddball motorist keeps away from the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an amusing oddity of a person, an informal noun for a character.
